items.title: Stem-and-Leaf Diagrams
items.body: Display raw data in order. Back-to-back stem plots compare two datasets. Median and quartiles easy to read.

items.title: Box-and-Whisker Plots
items.body: Shows minimum, Q1, median, Q3, maximum. IQR = Q3 − Q1. Outliers: values outside \(Q_1-1.5\times IQR\) or \(Q_3+1.5\times IQR\).

items.title: Histograms
items.body: Frequency density = frequency ÷ class width. Area of bar represents frequency. Used for continuous grouped data.

items.title: Cumulative Frequency
items.body: Ogive (cumulative frequency curve). Read median at \(n/2\), Q1 at \(n/4\), Q3 at \(3n/4\).

items.title: Measures of Location
items.body: Mean \(\bar{x}=\dfrac{\sum fx}{\sum f}\), Median (middle value), Mode (most frequent). For grouped data use midpoint.

items.title: Measures of Spread
items.body: Range, IQR, Variance \(\sigma^2=\dfrac{\sum fx^2}{n}-\bar{x}^2\), Standard deviation \(\sigma\).

body.en: For grouped data with \(n\) values: mean \(\bar{x}=\dfrac{\sum fx}{\sum f}\); variance \(\sigma^2=\dfrac{\sum fx^2}{\sum f}-\bar{x}^2\); standard deviation \(\sigma=\sqrt{\text{Var}}\). In a histogram (unequal class widths), plot frequency density \(=\text{freq}/\text{class width}\). In a cumulative frequency graph, the median is the \(\tfrac{n}{2}\)th value, \(Q_1\) is the \(\tfrac{n}{4}\)th, \(Q_3\) is the \(\tfrac{3n}{4}\)th.

label.en: ● Deep Conceptual Intuition — Representation of Data

body.en: Conditional Probability, Bayes' Theorem & Robust Summary Statistics: For any two events \(A\) and \(B\) with \(P(B) > 0\), conditional probability restricts the sample space to \(B\): \(P(A \mid B) = \dfrac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)}\). In descriptive statistics, the median and interquartile range (\(\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1\)) are resistant to extreme outliers, whereas the mean \(\bar{x}\) and standard deviation \(s\) are pulled strongly in the direction of skewness.

body.en:
Histograms with unequal class widths: The vertical axis must ALWAYS represent frequency density (\(\text{frequency} \div \text{class width}\)), never raw frequency. The area of each rectangle represents frequency.

Linear coding of data: If data values \(x\) are transformed via \(y = ax + b\):
• Mean scales and shifts: \(\bar{y} = a\bar{x} + b\)
• Variance scales by \(a^2\) only: \(\text{Var}(y) = a^2\text{Var}(x)\) (the additive constant \(b\) does not affect spread)
• Standard deviation scales by \(|a|\): \(\sigma_y = |a|\sigma_x\).

Variance formula accuracy: When calculating \(\sigma^2 = \frac{\sum x^2}{n} - \bar{x}^2\), never round \(\bar{x}\) prematurely before squaring; keep exact fractions or high precision to avoid severe cancellation errors.

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Representation of Data)

body.en:
Why Bayes' Theorem & Principle of Inclusion-Exclusion Work: Any event \(B\) can be partitioned into disjoint intersections \(B = (B \cap A) \cup (B \cap A')\). By additivity of mutually exclusive events and the multiplication rule \(P(A \cap B) = P(B \mid A)P(A)\):

\[ P(A \mid B) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)} = \frac{P(B \mid A)P(A)}{P(B \mid A)P(A) + P(B \mid A')P(A')} \]

Similarly, in counting \(|A \cup B|\), summing \(|A| + |B|\) counts every element in \(A \cap B\) twice; subtracting \(|A \cap B|\) once restores exact cardinality: \(P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B)\).

caption.en: Error Diagnosis — Common Student Traps vs. Exam-Board Method (Representation of Data)

rows.en: Using \(P(A \cap B) = 0\) when told \(A\) and \(B\) are independent
Confuses disjoint (mutually exclusive) events with statistically independent events.
For independent events, multiply probabilities: \(P(A \cap B) = P(A)\cdot P(B)\).
Dividing by the grand total \(N\) when computing \(P(A \mid B)\) from a table
Computes the joint probability \(P(A \cap B)\) instead of conditioning on subset \(B\).
Restrict the denominator strictly to the row/column total of the given condition \(B\).
Using permutations \({}^nP_r\) when selecting a committee with no distinct roles
Overcounts every group of size \(r\) by \(r!\) internal orderings.

label.en: ▲ Exam Pacing & Verification Strategy — Representation of Data

body.en: Exam Strategy (Cambridge International AS Level (9709 Paper 1 / Paper 4 / Paper 5)): Whenever a probability problem involves "at least one" success across multiple trials, immediately use the Complement Rule: \(P(\text{at least one}) = 1 - P(\text{none})\). It turns a multi-case sum into a single calculation.

question.en: A data set has mean 12 and standard deviation 4. A new value of 20 is added to \(n=9\) existing values. Without finding the new variance, find the new mean.
question.ar: A data set has mean 12 and standard deviation 4. A new value of 20 is added to \(n=9\) existing values. Without أوجدing the new variance, أوجد new mean.

solution.ar: خطوات الحل التفصيلية: Old sum \(=9\times12=108\). New sum \(=108+20=128\). New mean \(=128/10=12.8\).

hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(=9\times12=108\) لتبسيط الخطوة.
تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(=108+20=128\) لتبسيط الخطوة.
تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(= 128/10\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

question.en: A continuous dataset is grouped into class intervals. The interval \(20 \le x < 35\) has a frequency of 45. Find the frequency density for this class.
question.ar: A continuous dataset is grouped into class intervals. The interval \(20 \le x < 35\) has a frequency of 45. أوجد frequency density for this class.

solution.en: Class width \(w = 35 - 20 = 15\). Frequency density \(= \frac{\text{frequency}}{\text{class width}} = \frac{45}{15} = 3.0\). In a histogram, the height of the bar drawn on the interval \([20, 35)\) is 3.0.
solution.ar: خطوات الحل التفصيلية: Class width \(w = 35 - 20 = 15\). Frequency density \(= \frac{\text{frequency}}{\text{class width}} = \frac{45}{15} = 3.0\). In a histogram, the height of the bar drawn on the interval \([20, 35)\) is 3.0.

hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(w = 35 - 20\) لتبسيط الخطوة.
تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(\frac{\text{frequency}}{\text{class width}} = \frac{45}{15}\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

question.ar: [Practice 3 · Hard] أوجد discriminant of \( 5x^2-6x-3=0 \) and state the number of real roots.

hints.ar: جهّز الصيغة أو العبارة الرياضية: \(\Delta = b^2-4ac\).

hints.en: Substitute and simplify: \(\Delta = (-6)^2-4(5)(-3)\). Compute the final value from: \((-6)^2-4(5)(-3)\).
